title: Console Guided Onboarding Checklist — Rollout Plan (Phase 1 / Hosted API) — 2026-02
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-18 (Marissa)

Purpose
This doc defines the rollout plan for the Console “Guided Onboarding Checklist” (Phase 1: Hosted API / self-serve). It covers: feature flag strategy, cohorting/phased exposure, monitoring & alerting, operational procedures (enable/disable), and rollback.

Scope
- In scope: Console checklist UI + backend state, validation signals for key steps (first successful request, first streaming session, visited usage dashboard, prod-mode key created), and onboarding telemetry events.
- Out of scope: Dedicated/Private onboarding, SSO/SAML onboarding, automated validation for all production readiness items.

Owners / escalation
- DRI (product rollout): Marissa Cole
- Eng DRI (Console): Dylan Brooks
- Backend state DRI: Chloe Martin
- Telemetry pipeline DRI: Nadia Rahman
- Dashboards / analytics DRI: Mei Lin
- Security/privacy review: Marcus Lin (+ Legal: Michael Grant as needed)
- Support enablement: Dev Patel

Rollout principles (what we’re optimizing for)
1) Safety first: ability to turn off instantly (kill switch) with minimal user impact.
2) Learn quickly: early cohort should be biased toward high-signal users (new orgs + allowlist), but not so narrow that we miss real-world issues.
3) Stable measurement: telemetry must be correct before scaling exposure.
4) No privacy regressions: no prompt/user content in onboarding telemetry; strict property allowlist.

Feature flags
Flag name(s)
- Primary: console.guided_onboarding_checklist_v1
- Optional sub-flags (if we need staged functionality):
  - console.guided_onboarding_checklist_validations_v1 (step validation / auto-complete)
  - console.guided_onboarding_checklist_deeplinks_v1 (docs deep links + UTM)

Evaluation location
- Flag evaluated server-side (recommended): ensures consistent experience + prevents client tampering.
- Client reads “shouldShowChecklist” from Console bootstrap/config endpoint.

Targeting rules (in priority order)
1) Admin override allow/deny
- Console internal admin page supports:
  - force_on for org_id / project_id
  - force_off for org_id / project_id
  - reset checklist state (support/debug only)

2) Explicit allowlist (Beta)
- allowlist_org_ids: [list maintained by PM + Eng]
- allowlist_project_ids: optional for internal dogfood

3) New orgs only (default for early rollout)
- Definition: org_created_at >= rollout_start_date AND org plan is self-serve (no enterprise contract)
- Rationale: prevents confusing existing users and reduces “why did my UI change?” noise during beta.

4) Percentage rollout
- Deterministic hashing on org_id for stable membership
- percent_rollout: 0–100

Exclusions (hard blocks)
- If org is under “regulated/locked down mode” (privacy constraints or account flags from Security/Legal), default off unless explicitly allowlisted.
- If telemetry pipeline health is red (see Monitoring section), freeze or roll back percentage expansion.

Phased exposure plan
Phase 0 — Internal dogfood (1–3 days)
- Target: Redwood internal org(s) only
- Goals:
  - smoke test UI states, step transitions, deep links, and state persistence
  - verify no Console perf regressions (page load, API calls)
  - validate telemetry is flowing end-to-end
- Flag config:
  - percent_rollout=0
  - allowlist_org_ids=[Redwood internal]
- Exit criteria:
  - no P0s in first 48 hours
  - telemetry event volume matches expected (within +/-20%)

Phase 1 — Limited beta (allowlist + 5% new orgs)
- Duration: ~1 week (or until we hit ~200–500 new orgs, whichever is later)
- Target: allowlisted beta customers + small random sample of new orgs
- Goals:
  - identify confusing copy/ordering
  - ensure validators behave with real traffic and expected lag
  - catch support-impact issues (401/429 confusion, streaming disconnect paths)
- Flag config:
  - allowlist_org_ids=[beta cohort]
  - percent_rollout=5 (new orgs)
- Required comms:
  - Support macro draft referencing new checklist + troubleshooting doc
  - Release note marked “Beta” (internal + optionally public docs note)
- Exit criteria:
  - no sustained increase in support tickets attributed to checklist (>10% week-over-week for onboarding categories)
  - validator lag is within expected bounds (see Validator notes)

Phase 2 — Expanded beta (20% new orgs)
- Duration: 1–2 weeks
- Goals:
  - validate funnel improvements at scale (TTFS, completion)
  - ensure infra/telemetry scale and alerting stability
- Flag config:
  - percent_rollout=20 (new orgs)
- Exit criteria:
  - telemetry missing-event rate < 0.5% across regions
  - error budget: no increase in Console 5xx attributable to checklist endpoints

Phase 3 — Pre-GA (50% new orgs)
- Duration: 1 week
- Goals:
  - final copy and docs alignment
  - confirm Support readiness and operational playbooks
- Flag config:
  - percent_rollout=50 (new orgs)
- Exit criteria:
  - stakeholder signoff: Product (Marissa/Nikhil), Design (Tessa), DevEx Docs (Elliot), SDK (Monica), Security (Marcus)

Phase 4 — GA (100% new orgs)
- Default experience for newly created orgs/projects.
- Post-GA follow-up: discuss enabling for existing orgs after we confirm it doesn’t confuse established workflows.

Phase 5 — Existing orgs (TBD)
- Not planned for Phase 1. If we decide to do it:
  - introduce “Dismiss / Hide checklist” control
  - avoid forcing checklist onto accounts created before launch
  - focus on accounts that haven’t made a successful request yet

Validator notes (known constraints)
First successful request
- Signal source: gateway logs/metrics aggregated per project.
- Expected lag: 1–5 minutes typical; can be up to 15 minutes in worst-case during pipeline lag.
- UX behavior:
  - Step can show “We’ll auto-detect this (may take a few minutes)”
  - Provide manual “I’ve made a request” link to troubleshooting/quickstart, but do NOT mark complete based on self-attestation.

First streaming session
- Edge cases: disconnects, retries, partial streams.
- Definition (current): any streaming response that delivers >= 1 data chunk after headers, associated with a project.

Visited usage dashboard
- Client-side event only, no sensitive props.

Prod-mode API key created
- Requires Console API key UI differentiation (test vs prod labeling).
- If we can’t reliably validate, keep as “recommended/manual” for beta and add validation post-GA.

Monitoring & dashboards
Telemetry health (must-have)
- Dashboard: “Onboarding Telemetry Health”
  - event ingestion volume by region
  - lag (p50/p95) from event_emitted_at -> event_ingested_at
  - missing required properties rate (schema violations)
  - dedupe collision rate (should be near zero)
- Alerts:
  - Missing events from any region for >10 minutes
  - Ingestion lag p95 > 15 minutes for >30 minutes
  - Schema violation rate > 1% for >15 minutes

Product funnel dashboards (must-have)
- “Checklist Funnel (v1)” by cohort and time
  - Step completion rate per step
  - Drop-off per step
  - Median time-to-first-success (signup/org_created -> first_success)
  - Median time-to-streaming
  - Correlation to D7 activation (proxy: repeat usage / token spend)
- Breakdowns:
  - region
  - SDK language (if we have it via docs UTM or SDK user agent)
  - plan tier

Console / backend health
- Checklist endpoints:
  - latency p50/p95
  - 4xx/5xx rate
  - error logs sampled (no sensitive payloads)
- Console performance:
  - page load metrics for onboarding surfaces

Go / no-go checklist for expanding rollout
Before moving from 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%
- Telemetry health is green for 72 hours
- No open P0/P1 bugs tagged “checklist-rollout”
- Support has updated macros + knows how to disable checklist / reset state for affected orgs
- Docs deep links verified (no 404s; correct UTM conventions)
- Security signoff that property allowlist is enforced and prompt content is not captured

Operational procedures
How to enable
- Update flag config in feature-flag service:
  - set allowlist_org_ids
  - set percent_rollout
  - ensure targeting is new_orgs_only=true for phases 1–4
- Confirm in Console:
  - org in cohort sees checklist component on landing surface
  - state persists on reload
  - at least one telemetry “checklist_viewed” event is observed

How to disable (soft rollback)
- Set percent_rollout=0 and clear allowlist_org_ids (or keep allowlist only for internal testing).
- Keep backend endpoints live (no need to deploy) to avoid errors for users mid-session.
- Expected user impact: checklist disappears; users can continue using Console as before.

Full rollback (code rollback)
Use only if disabling the flag is insufficient (e.g., severe perf regression due to background calls).
- Roll back Console release train to prior version.
- Roll back backend deploy if endpoints are causing load/issues.
- Validate:
  - no elevated 5xx
  - no runaway retries from client

Data / state considerations during rollback
- Checklist state is safe to keep even if the feature is disabled.
- When re-enabled, state should resume.
- If we change step IDs between versions, we must provide a migration mapping (avoid “stuck steps”).

Incident playbook (during beta)
If an alert fires for missing onboarding events or ingestion lag:
1) Freeze rollout expansion (do not increase percentage).
2) If the issue is regional and impacts validators (e.g., first success detection):
   - temporarily show “manual guidance” UI state (if supported), otherwise disable validations sub-flag.
3) If issue affects Console stability/perf: disable primary flag.
4) Notify #eng-releases and #eng-sre with status + next update ETA.

Comms plan
Internal
- Weekly beta update in Product/Eng sync (funnel, top issues, next cohort change)
- Release train notes for flag changes (date/time, percent, cohort definition)

External (beta users)
- Minimal, targeted:
  - message sent to allowlisted beta customers when enabled (what’s new, how to give feedback)
  - link to troubleshooting page and how to contact support

Open questions (as of 2026-02-18)
- Do we need a user-visible “Dismiss checklist” control during Phase 1, or only when we consider existing-org rollout?
- Do we want the checklist shown at org level or project level by default? (Current assumption: project-context checklist with org-level onboarding entry point.)
- What is the final GA definition for “production launch” steps vs “recommended best practices”? (Tracked in PM-483/PM-486.)

Appendix: Quick reference
- Kill switch: set console.guided_onboarding_checklist_v1 percent_rollout=0
- Beta cohort owner: Marissa (updates allowlist)
- Telemetry DRI on-call: Nadia
- Support reset request: Internal ticket (INT-3309 pattern) + admin reset tool
